outcome: maternal morbidity/mortality (blood transfusion rates, hysterectomy rates)
laboratory results (platelet count, prothrombin time, fibrinogen level)
cohort: Patients with a pregnancy modified DIC score >= 26, identified from 154,233 deliveries at a single center due to obstetric conditions such as obstetric bleeding, placental abruption, or preeclampsia/HELLP syndrome.
finding: In patients with DIC, preeclampsia/HELLP syndrome as the underlying cause is associated with a distinct laboratory profile (lower platelet count, lower prothrombin time, higher fibrinogen level) and better maternal outcomes (lower rates of blood transfusion and hysterectomy) compared to obstetric hemorrhage or placental abruption.
